## Summary

**PERM** (Permute): Change order and place in destination.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `Pick bytes from a & b→ b` |
| Syntax | `PERM #n,Ra,Rb`<br>Where #n contains the picking order from a & b. |
| Short | Change order and place in destination. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–4 | `010011001100` |
| 1 | 3–0 | a |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–9 | pos0 |
| 2 | 8–6 | pos1 |
| 2 | 5–3 | pos2 |
| 2 | 2–0 | pos3 |

- a & b=0..7 data register 8..15 address register
- data-registers can be banked so a & b includes En.

### Example

```asm
    perm    #@3325,a0,e1
```

```text
a a0: .. .. .. .. 00 11 22 33
b e1: .. .. .. .. 44 55 66 77
Result:
b e1: .. .. .. .. 33 33 22 55
```

### Notes

- Banked address registers are not supported, they show up as En when banked.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no PERM. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T bank address registers in PERM: they show up as En.
